unit: H4 — the second scan of vol. II, targeted, as a witness
what_this_is: THE READINGS TAKEN FROM A SECOND PHYSICAL COPY OF VOL. II, with their provenance. NO PAGE IMAGE OF ANY THIRD-PARTY SCAN IS HELD OR COMMITTED — only these texts, exactly as the edition holds the Project Gutenberg volumes as witness TEXT.

witnesses_used.what: a complete copy of vol. II of the 1816 print, digitised by Google for the University of Michigan
witnesses_used.rights: HathiTrust rightsCode pd, "Full view"; catalogue record 002240527
witnesses_used.route: r.jina.ai screenshot of the babel viewer -> 302 signed Google Storage PNG (1280x1280); the direct image, plaintext and PDF endpoints are 403 and a plain curl of the viewer meets Cloudflare
route_defects: the first capture is often the viewer's loading placeholder and r.jina.ai CACHES BY URL, so that placeholder is served forever for that page: MEASURED, seq 237 (printed p.227) returned the placeholder 8/8 times until an ignored query parameter busted the cache
the cookie modal covers the foot of every page in a fresh browser context, so the last one or two printed lines are not available at all

witnesses_used.crop_proof: MEASURED on three pages (printed 18, 226, 227): with this box the page's own ink inside the crop has margins of at least 77 px left, 72 px right and 96 px top on all three, so no printed line is cut at those edges; the BOTTOM is the exception and is the cookie modal, not a tuning error
witnesses_used.terms_of_service_rule: ONE PAGE PER DECISION (only the pages a decision needs are fetched); requests are paced (>= 4 s apart); every request carries an identifying User-Agent; NO HathiTrust PAGE IMAGE IS WRITTEN INTO THIS REPOSITORY — what is held is the READINGS, as below.

witnesses_used.name: taylor-theology-of-plato-en-t.-2-1816
witnesses_used.what: an INDEPENDENT scan of the same 1816 vol. II, whose OCR text this edition SERVED until 2026-10-05
witnesses_used.its_page_images: native 4792 x 6275 (3.4x the linear resolution of this edition's own stored scans), fetched from archive.org one page at a time by leaf for the pages a decision needed
witnesses_used.the_defect_this_unit_found: that witness record carries NO model block, so NO page-based measurement has ever used it: tools/witness-unsure.mjs selects copies by w.model (only the two vol-I copies have one) and tools/pg-locate.mjs uses only the re-flowed Gutenberg volumes. MEASURED: zero of the 22 committed tools/edits/<slug>.*.json artifacts cite it, and the H2b-ii artifact ocr-copy-verdicts.json records counts.placed_in_vol_I=470 of 809 flagged OCR rules — that measurement was scoped to vol. I.

targets_worked.definition: every vol. II rule whose reading is GREEK (type transliteration), is still review-flagged, and rests on exactly ONE instrument (MEASURED: 40 rules, all of them `google/gemini-2.5-flash`) — the class a second scan of the same print is uniquely able to corroborate or refute
targets_worked.method: the printed page is placed in the second scan by the page's OWN content (rare-word match against the leaf's own OCR, searched in a window around the page number), the leaf is fetched at NATIVE resolution, the rule's own printed line is located from the leaf's OWN word boxes anchored on the rule's English, and that band (and the page's footnote zone) is read BLIND by two readers. The candidate reading is never shown to a reader.

the_instrument_measurement_that_decides_.test: THREE draws of ONE reader (Qwen/Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct) on ONE image — the second scan's native-resolution band of printed p.227, the page whose print sets "ορουω and θειω" — with ONE prompt, run back to back
draws: "σπουδην και θεσιν" (a reading of a DIFFERENT printed line, quoted by the reader as "Orithya, also, may be said...")
the_instrument_measurement_that_decides_.result: THE THREE DRAWS DISAGREE WITH EACH OTHER and not one of them is the print's own reading — at confidence "high" every time. A different prompt on the SAME image had earlier returned the print's reading exactly ("ορουω θειω").
the_instrument_measurement_that_decides_.consequence: a single draw of these readers is NOT a reading on this print's small Greek. Under this library's own rule (two instruments must agree where a reading is at stake; a tie or a single reader licenses nothing), that is enough to refuse every verdict below — and it is the reason this unit changes no reading.

the_two_routes_compared_head_to_head.pages: printed p.82 and printed p.227, both fetched BOTH ways and read by BOTH readers with the same prompt
the_two_routes_compared_head_to_head.second_scan_native: p.227: the print's Greek recovered ("ορουω θειω" on one prompt; the three-draw probe above shows the instability). p.82: both readers agreed on the page's footnote Greek, e.g. "τα παραγοντα, τα παραοντα" unaccented as printed
the_two_routes_compared_head_to_head.hathitrust_render: p.82 AND p.227: BOTH readers returned ZERO Greek lines (the running head was read correctly, so the image itself was legible — the Greek is not recoverable at this resolution). The crop IS known to contain p.227's Greek line: this unit read it there with its own eyes.
the_two_routes_compared_head_to_head.conclusion: the HathiTrust route cannot settle the class it was aimed at. Its honest role is what is left: a third observation, at a resolution that decides Latin words and ordinary punctuation, and nothing finer.
